per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: How are starting properties and money assigned, where do the dealt cards go, and how is the End of Game card inserted?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p2 Setting Up; unified p5

required_fact_review.fact: Remove End of Game, shuffle, deal two property cards per player.
Mark the two initial lots and take starting money equal to the sum of their printed card money values.
Discard by color/Strip with counts visible.
Divide remaining shuffled deck into four roughly equal stacks; End of Game on top of fourth, other three on top.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Actual setup-property/money/card/deck questions match all four required clauses; setup-only reuse restriction remains context.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: Who takes the first turn, how does turn order proceed, and what is the normal Draw/Play sequence?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p2 Taking Turns/On Every Turn; p3 Ending Step 1

required_fact_review.fact: Each rolls two dice; highest roller takes player card and first turn.
Pass player card left after each turn.
Draw property card, take its lot, pay all owned lots, pay/score indicated casinos, discard appropriately, then Play actions.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: First actor, left handoff, and full normal Draw/Play ordering are asked; no invented first-roll tie procedure.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: You draw the card for an empty lot. When is it acquired and paid, and do the printed card starting-money values pay again?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p2 Setting Up/Take Over Your Lot/Owned Lots Pay

required_fact_review.fact: Place your marker before payouts.
The newly acquired marked lot pays you $1 in the coming lot payout.
Card money values are used only during setup, not drawn-turn income.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Claims, immediate new-lot payment and setup-only card money are directly asked; other marked lots remain context.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: You draw a lot card for a sprawled tile with an opponent’s 5, although the board prints 2. What happens to the tile and die, and who receives its imminent matching-color money?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p2 Take Over Your Lot/Money Paid

required_fact_review.fact: Tile stays; replace opposing die with your own retaining current value 5, not printed 2.
Acquisition precedes payouts, so you receive $5 for that die when its casino pays.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Replacement/current value, unchanged tile and immediate matching income are directly asked.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: When do same-color tiles form one casino, can they be divided, and is the boss determined by total pips or something else?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p1 Casino Tiles/Player Dice; p2 Who Owns What

required_fact_review.fact: Edge-connected same-color tiles on same block form a single indivisible casino; diagonal-only contact does not.
Boss is owner of highest individual die, not greatest total pips or most tiles.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Connected casino identity, indivisibility and highest individual die are asked; this does not directly ask the definition of a lot or whether an ownerless tile can be sprawled over.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: A three-tile gold casino contains Red 5 and Blue 3 and 2; Red also owns two marked lots. On a gold payout, how much money and how many points does each receive from these holdings?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p2 Owned Lots Pay/Money Paid/Points Earned

required_fact_review.fact: Red receives $7: $5 die plus $2 lots.
Blue receives $5 from dice.
Red boss receives 3 casino points, Blue no casino points.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: All $7/$5 and 3/0-point outcomes correctly follow pips/marked lots/boss, and are asked.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: How does Pay The Strip differ from a color payout, and what qualifies a casino whose only one tile touches The Strip?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p2 Pay Based on Color/Pay The Strip; unified p8

required_fact_review.fact: Color pays all casinos of that color anywhere.
Strip pays all colors with at least one casino edge adjacent to Strip.
Entire qualifying casino pays money/points for all tiles, not only touching tile.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Color-versus-Strip scope and whole qualifying casino payment are directly asked.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: Which actions may you take in Play, in what order and how often, and may another player perform an action on your turn?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p3 Step 2 Play/Reorganize; p4 Trading

required_fact_review.fact: Build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize, gamble in any order.
All may repeat except gamble once per own turn; reorganization also limited per die per turn.
No player takes actions on another player’s turn.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Base action list, order, repetition/reorg limitation and no off-turn action are asked; trading context is not an extra fact.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: How do you build on your marked lot whose board price is $6 and printed die is 2? State cost, marker and die handling, and tile choice.
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p3 Build; unified p10 Build

required_fact_review.fact: Pay $6; choose available casino tile color.
Remove/reclaim marker, place tile and your die set to printed board value2.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Execution cost/marker/die/tile choice are asked; supplied ownership and absent-neighbor merger correctly remain context.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: You boss a gold casino and want to sprawl onto an edge-adjacent empty unowned $9 lot with printed die 3. What do you pay and place, and may you instead sprawl onto an opponent’s marked lot or a merely diagonal lot?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p3 Sprawl

required_fact_review.fact: Pay $18, place available gold tile with own die 3.
required_fact_review.asked_scope: supported; see entry note for supplied-context qualification

required_fact_review.fact: The stated eligible lot is empty/unowned and edge-adjacent; opponent-marked and diagonal-only targets are illegal.
required_fact_review.asked_scope: supported; see entry note for supplied-context qualification

required_fact_review.fact: Cannot sprawl without available tile of same color.
required_fact_review.asked_scope: supported; see entry note for supplied-context qualification

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: $18, same-color placement at die3, opponent-marker rejection, diagonal rejection and available matching tile are source-correct. However emptiness of the stated target is given; the question does not ask the occupied-but-ownerless target branch. Do not make repetition of the empty given an extra scoring demand.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: How does remodeling a two-tile casino work, including eligibility, cost, tile supply, and a merger with a neighboring casino whose highest die beats yours?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p3 Remodel and example; unified p11

required_fact_review.fact: Must boss casino; remodel all its tiles into one new color with enough available tiles.
Pay $10 ($5 each); replace all tiles with new-color tiles; dice/holdings remain.
Edge-adjacent same-color casinos merge; owner of larger die becomes boss even if another player.
Return replaced old-color tiles to their supply.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Eligibility, whole-casino color change, $10, tile sufficiency/return and superior opponent die after merger are within asked procedure.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: May a non-boss with one die reorganize a casino with dice 5, 3 and 2? State who pays how much, which dice roll and who rolls them, and where multiple dice may return.
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p3 Reorganize

required_fact_review.fact: Yes, at least one own die suffices; acting player pays $10 total pips of all dice.
All dice reroll, each owner rolling their own.
Each owner returns dice only to their own original tiles, choosing assignment among those tiles if multiple.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Non-boss own-die eligibility, acting payer/all pips, every owner rolling and original-tile permutation are directly asked.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: A die was reorganized earlier this turn and its casino then merges into a larger casino. Can the larger casino be reorganized this turn, and are free boss-tie rerolls prohibited too?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p3 Reorganize; p4 Reroll if Tied; unified p11

required_fact_review.fact: No: no die may be reorganized more than once per turn, so any previously reorganized die prevents reorganization of the enlarged casino.
Boss-tie rerolls are free and not subject to reorganization once-per-turn limit.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Enlarged casino blocked by already-reorganized die; free boss tie rolling remains allowed. Both are asked.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: After a merger, Red 5 and Blue 5 tie above Green 4. What rerolls, at what cost, and who bosses if both 5s reroll to 3? What if all largest tied dice belong to one player, or only smaller dice tie?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p4 After Each Action Reroll if Tied and diagram

required_fact_review.fact: Immediately reroll only tied largest dice at no cost.
If both become 3, Green unchanged 4 is boss; do not keep rerolling smaller 3s.
Same-player highest tie requires no reroll; ties below highest require none.
If different players remain tied for current highest, repeat with current highest until one player controls highest.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Immediate/current-highest/free rolling, unchanged third-player winner and same-player/lower ties are asked. Iteration explains complete tie resolution.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: You have $18 and gamble at an opponent’s four-tile casino whose boss has $15. What is the maximum bet, who gets the House card, and how many times may you gamble this turn?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p4 Gamble

required_fact_review.fact: Maximum $15: minimum of $20 tile cap, own $18 and boss $15.
Gamble once during own turn.
Give the casino boss the House card.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: $15 minimum cap, House recipient and once-per-turn are asked; opponent-boss status is supplied context.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: For a legal $4 bet against a boss who has $7, resolve every possible two-dice sum group, including the limited doubled payout. Is a winning bettor also losing their stake?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p4 Gamble; unified p13

required_fact_review.fact: 3/4/9/10/11: win $4 from boss and retain/get stake back.
2/12: nominal win $8 but receive only boss’s available $7 and retain/get stake back.
5/6/7/8: lose/pay $4 to boss.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: All three complete dice-sum groups, doubled insolvency and returned stake are directly asked and correct.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: What may be traded, when may trading occur, how are traded lots and dice transferred, and what cannot be promised or traded?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p4 Trading; unified physicalp9 Settling Who’s the Boss, physicalp15 Trading, physicalp16 Winning.

required_fact_review.fact: Trade money, lots, casino dice and actions on the active player’s current turn. Trading may occur even off-turn, except no initiated trades during unresolved boss ties or after End of Game is drawn.
Replace lot marker with recipient marker; replace die with recipient die at same current pip value, not board value.
No points or casino tiles; no promises of future-turn actions/exchanges/transfers.
No actions on another player’s turn.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Broad what/when/how/restrictions wording supports permitted assets/current active actions, transfer values, two timing exceptions and future-turn ban. Corrected unifiedp9/p15/p16 references support those exceptions.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: Starting at score 8, where do single casino awards of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 points leave you? Can two separate one-tile casinos combine their awards, and in what order are different casinos scored?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p2 Scoring; p3 scoring example and multiple casinos

required_fact_review.fact: 1 leaves 8; 2 or 3 reaches 10; 4 or 5 reaches 12.
Insufficient excess at a break is lost; cannot pool separate casino awards.
Score each casino independently smallest to largest, player chooses equal-size order; two single-tile awards leave 8.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: All score8 numeric outcomes, lost excess, separate awards and ascending order match asked clauses.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: What happens when the End of Game card is drawn, including remaining actions, final payouts, winner and tied score? Is there an immediate alternative win condition?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p4 Winning; unified p16

required_fact_review.fact: Game ends immediately; no subsequent Play actions.
Final payout all owned lots and casinos touching Strip, with ordinary money and scoring rules.
Most points wins; tied most points breaks by most money.
90+ points wins immediately in base game.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Immediate end, no Play, final lots/Strip, score/money comparison and original-base90+ win match asked clauses. Expansion end-point amendments correctly excluded.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: In two-player play, what happens to F cards drawn during setup and during a turn? May anyone build on F, and can a turn pay more than once before actions?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p4 2-Player Rules/Winning; unified p16 2-Player Rules

required_fact_review.fact: No building on F block.
Setup F card is discarded and replaced; valid two cards determine initial properties/money.
During turn do not mark F; pay owned lots and indicated casinos/points, discard then repeat Draw until A–E card resolved.
Each such draw pays, so multiple payouts occur in one turn before Play.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: F setup discard/replacement, no F building/marker, repeated payouts/discard before actions are asked. End interruption remains tested elsewhere.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: All nine gold tiles are on the board. Can you build another gold tile using the spare tenth tile, sprawl a gold casino, or remodel a three-tile casino to gold? May you build a different available color?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p1 Casino Tiles; p3 Available Tiles/Build/Sprawl/Remodel

required_fact_review.fact: The tenth is a replacement, not a tenth usable tile.
Cannot build gold, sprawl gold or remodel to gold without sufficient available tiles.
Yes, a different available color may be built on an owned lot.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Replacement tenth tile, unavailable color across three actions and another available color are directly asked; no invented price required.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: All twelve of your dice are on the board when you build, sprawl or inherit a sprawled tile. How do you place the required die, what happens to the vacated tile and its scoring, and what if it was the casino’s only die?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p3 Available Dice; unified p6 Available Dice

required_fact_review.fact: Remove one of your existing ownership dice and place it on the new tile at the value required by the placement.
Vacated tile remains ownerless but counts for casino points.
If no dice remain in a casino it has no owner/boss.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Forced relocation, persisting ownerless tile/scoring and no boss after last die are directly asked. It does not ask the legality of placing another tile over the vacated tile.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: A property draw claims a sprawled casino tile with no die; the board prints 2, while the die removed from it used to be 5. What die do you place, does the tile change, and when does its matching casino pay?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p2 Take Over Your Lot/Money Paid; unified p7

required_fact_review.fact: Place own die at printed board value 2; former removed value 5 is not retained.
Casino tile remains; acquisition precedes matching casino payment.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Printed-value die placement, persisting tile and takeover-before-payout are asked; numerical $2 income is correctly background.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: You draw the card for your own sprawled tile, whose die is now 6 although the board prints 2. Does ownership or value change, and what does that die earn if its casino pays?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Unified p7 Step 2; original p2 Money Paid

required_fact_review.fact: Leave your existing die unchanged at 6.
Matching payout pays you $6 for that die.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Existing own die stays6 and pays$6; both asked.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: All ten of your markers are on lots and you acquire another empty lot. How is ownership marked, what happens to the vacated lot, and which of the two lots receives the coming owned-lot payout?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Unified p6 Available Player Markers; original p2 Draw/Owned Lots Pay

required_fact_review.fact: Move one existing marker to newly gained lot.
You no longer own vacated lot; it does not pay you lot income.
New marked lot pays you $1 in upcoming payout.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Marker relocation, old lot loses ownership/payout and new lot pays$1 are directly asked.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: May a player conceal money or piece counts, forbid inspection of a discard pile, or deny a bank payout because the physical bank is empty?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p1 Money; unified p6 Your Resources/Available Money

required_fact_review.fact: Money, piece counts and discarded cards are public; anyone may inspect discards.
Bank money unlimited; physical bank exhaustion does not cancel a payout.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Public money/pieces/discards and unlimited bank are directly asked.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: A casino has two Red 6s and a Blue 3. During a trade one Red 6 is replaced by Green’s die. What value does Green’s die have, must anything reroll before further trades or actions, and who rolls?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p4 Trading/Reroll if Tied; unified p9 Settling Who’s the Boss

required_fact_review.fact: Green replacement remains 6.
Different players now tie for highest: immediately reroll both highest 6s (remaining Red and new Green), not Blue3.
Each owner rolls own tied dice; finish resolving current-highest cross-player ties before actions or initiating trades.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Current6 transfer, highest cross-player rolling, owner rollers and resolution before further initiated trades/actions are asked; cost remains context.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: You draw a card and replace one of Red’s tied highest 5s in a casino with your own 5; another Red 5 remains. Is the boss tie postponed until after payment or Play, and does this reroll count as a paid reorganization?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Unified p7 Step 2/p9 Settling Who’s the Boss; p11 Reorganize

required_fact_review.fact: Resolve cross-player highest tie immediately on takeover before casino payouts, not postponed to Play.
Reroll only current highest dice free; this is not paid reorganization and does not use its limit.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Takeover tie immediately before payment and free/non-reorganization status are asked.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: May you reorganize a casino where you alone own all dice, or one where you own none? Does reorganizing only one of your dice avoid paying for the opponents’ pips?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p3 Reorganize; unified p11

required_fact_review.fact: Sole owner may reorganize; no-own-die casino may not.
Reorganization always rerolls every die and costs all pips, including opponents, not just selected own dice.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Sole-owner/no-own-die eligibility and prohibition on partial dice/cost are asked.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: All twelve of your ownership dice are on casino tiles. Must you remove a tile’s die just to gamble, and may you gamble at your own casino if no opponent bosses any casino?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Unified p6 Available Dice; p13 Gamble

required_fact_review.fact: Any dice may be used to gamble; no ownership placement or removal required for the gambling roll.
Cannot gamble at own casino; if no opponent bosses a casino there is no legal gambling action.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Any dice for gambling without ownership-die relocation and absent eligible opponent boss are asked.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: On your turn you trade for an opponent’s die so that you can reorganize their casino, then promise to pay them for a sprawl only if the reorganization gives you control. If the reroll does not make you boss so the agreed sprawl cannot happen, do the subsequent steps of the trade proceed? Could the opponent instead perform the sprawl on your turn?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Unified p15 Trading; original p3 Sprawl/p4 Trading

required_fact_review.fact: When an element of trade is prevented, subsequent steps do not occur.
Opponent cannot take action on your turn.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Only trade continuation and off-turn substitution are asked. Boss-control failure is explicitly given; corrected two-fact requirement and current-turn scope note are appropriate.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: The End of Game card has just been drawn. Before the final payout, may players initiate a last-minute trade of money or a casino die, perhaps to change who wins a tied score?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p4 Winning; unified physical p16 Winning, first paragraph (no actions or initiated trades on End of Game draw).

required_fact_review.fact: No: End of Game draw immediately ends play, so players cannot initiate a money/die trade before final payouts.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: No initiated last-minute trade after end draw is the only asked ruling; payout/winner recap correctly background.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: During setup, which pieces does each player take, and where is each player’s scoring chip placed before the first turn?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p2 Setting Up, first and third paragraphs; unified physical p5 Setting Up.

required_fact_review.fact: Each player takes an action card and the scoring chip, markers and dice of one player color. Place every player’s scoring chip on 0 on the scoring track.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Player aid and single-color pieces plus zero initial score are directly asked.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: Must a trade be between exactly two players, or may three players participate in one agreed trade of their money, lots and casino dice?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Unified physical p15 At Any Time: Trading, first paragraph: any number of players may be involved. Original p4 Trading supplies base assets and restrictions.

required_fact_review.fact: Any number of players may be involved in a trade, so a three-player trade is permitted, subject to the ordinary restrictions on traded assets and timing.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Any-number actor rule answers the explicit two-versus-three-player permission. No extra full trading recital required.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: Besides taking their own components, what banking role must the group assign during setup?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p2 Setting Up, second paragraph; unified physical p5 Setting Up.

required_fact_review.fact: Choose a player to be the Banker.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: Assign a player as Banker is precisely asked.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: You have a die in a casino, but another player is its boss. May you sprawl that casino during your own turn?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p3 Action–Sprawl; unified physicalp10 Sprawl.

required_fact_review.fact: No. Only the boss may sprawl a casino; merely owning a die is insufficient.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: New actual question directly asks non-boss Sprawl eligibility; source says boss only. Q10/Q31 previously gave this condition, so addition is novel.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.asked_question: May you use Build on an empty unowned lot or another player’s marked lot, or must the target be a lot you own?
per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.source_references: Original p3 Action–Build; unified physicalp10 Build.

required_fact_review.fact: Build may be used only on a lot you own. An unowned lot or another player’s marked lot is not a legal Build target.

per_question_asked_fact_and_key_review.reviewer_note: New actual question directly asks Build target ownership; source says only own lots. Q09 previously supplied this condition. This is a different action’s condition from Sprawl unowned targets.

findings.proposed_question: You boss a gold casino. An edge-adjacent purple casino tile has no die. May you pay double its printed lot price to sprawl gold onto that space, or must Sprawl use an empty lot?
findings.required_answer: No. Sprawl requires an empty, unowned lot. The purple casino tile remains on the board despite having no die; it is not a lot and cannot be covered or replaced by a Sprawl action.

source_evidence.exact_text: A lot is a space that does not contain a tile.

Once built, your 
casino is no longer treated as a lot.

on any empty, unowned lot with an edge adjacent 
to the sprawling casino.

The resulting tile without a die 
remains on the board. No one owns a tile without a die, 
though it still counts for points in the casino.

source_evidence.source: Unified physicalp6 Who Owns What / p10 Sprawl
source_evidence.support: A lot has no tile; built casino space ceases being a lot. Sprawl chooses an unowned neighboring lot without a marker, using the same casino color.

actual_asked_clause_comparison.asked: What do you pay/place on the specified empty unowned edge-adjacent lot, and may you instead use an opponent-marked or diagonal lot?
actual_asked_clause_comparison.missing: Emptiness is expressly supplied for the legal scenario. Ownership and adjacency exclusions are asked, but the occupied/unowned distinction is not.

actual_asked_clause_comparison.asked: Required die placement and what happens to the vacated tile/scoring and last-die casino ownership.
actual_asked_clause_comparison.missing: It asks tile persistence/ownership/scoring, not eligibility of that occupied space as a Sprawl target.

actual_asked_clause_comparison.asked: Die value, tile persistence and takeover timing when a property card claims a die-less tile.
actual_asked_clause_comparison.missing: Draw takeover is a different procedure; it does not ask legal Sprawl targets.

actual_asked_clause_comparison.asked: Casino connectivity, indivisibility and boss determination.
actual_asked_clause_comparison.missing: It does not ask the lot-versus-casino target distinction.

actual_asked_clause_comparison.asked: Build on unowned/opponent-marked lots versus own lots.
actual_asked_clause_comparison.missing: It directly tests Build ownership among lot targets, not Sprawl emptiness or whether an occupied ownerless tile qualifies as a lot.

findings.why_not_cosmetic: The target is an occupied but ownerless casino space, separating empty from unowned. Replacing one lot owner, coordinate, color or price cannot test this distinct predicate.
findings.why_not_merely_mechanical_recombination: The remaining target condition empty is not actually asked by Q10; it is only a given. Q22 establishes that a tile persists but asks no Sprawl permission. Combining already-asked outcomes cannot be used to declare the unasked empty-target precondition covered, under the same asked-versus-given standard that motivated Q36 and Q37.
findings.recommended_scope_handling: If accepted, add a separate explicitly versioned question/key/coverage entry without modifying existing question or baseline-answer records; reset zero-addition stopping passes after the accepted new branch. In Q10 do not treat repetition of its supplied empty-target context as an extra required fact.
